result.title: The Schatten-3 Lindelöf Lock: eigenvalue-tail bounds for the Weil–Gabor matrix at near-critical bandwidth and the unconditional cubic certificate
result.thesis: The Lindelöf lock does not need pointwise lambda_max = O(1): a Schatten-3 tail bound Sum_{|lambda_i| >= V0} |lambda_i|^3 = o(N) with V0 = polylog(T), provable NOW at bandwidth lambda = 1/2 + O(loglog T/log T) from classical mean values (Montgomery–Vaughan + a free unique-factorization fourth moment + Huxley large values), converts the unconditionally computable third trace tr G~^3 (Rudnick–Sarnak range, v5 §7.2(e)) into a sign-sensitive constraint that separates on-line doubles (cubic charge +8) from off-line pairs (cubic charge 0), breaking the lemmaR_tight degeneracy in a joint two-bandwidth LP whose counting still runs at lambda = 1.
result.mechanism:
OBJECTS. P_X(tau) = Sum_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-1/2-i tau}, X = T^lambda; equivalently A(tau) = Sum_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-1/2 - i tau} with mean square Sum Lambda(n)^2/n ~ L^2/2, L = lambda*l, l = log(T/2pi). G-hat = normalized Weil–Gabor matrix (units (4.4): isolated on-line zero -> eigenvalue m_rho, window-independent), d = lambda*N windows of width 2pi/L, eigenvalues lambda_i. Known unconditionally: tr G-hat = N(1+o(1)), tr G-hat^2 = (1/lambda + lambda/3)N, and — decisive, v5 §7.2(e) — tr G-hat^3 is evaluable by the §5 diagonal method exactly when X^3 <= T^{2-eps}, i.e. lambda < 2/3. The full lock lambda_max = O(1) is Lindelöf-strength (it is a pointwise bound on window-smoothed |P_X|, i.e. on ζ'/ζ near the line). Two structural no-gos frame the design: (a) §7.5(e): "an odd moment does not lower Lambda_1(0)" — because with UNBOUNDED spectral support, eigenvalue mass at height h -> infinity feeds m_3 freely (LP-dual: cubic certificate coefficients must have c_3 <= 0); (b) lemmaR_tight: from (tr, Frobenius, n_+, integer atoms) an on-line double (eigenvalue +2) and a tight off-line pair (eigenvalues ±2) both charge 4 and are indistinguishable. Both no-gos are evaded by the same object: a TAIL bound on the spectrum plus the SIGN of the third moment. A hyperbolic pair block contributes (+a)^3 + (-a)^3 = 0 to tr G-hat^3 while a double contributes +8: the odd moment is exactly the sign-sensitive datum the quadratic certificate lacks — but it is usable only if the spectral support is effectively bounded, which is the tail theorem.

STEP 1 — BRIDGE LEMMA (pure linear algebra, formalizable). Take phi in C^5 so the entries decay |G-hat_{kl}| <= C (1+|k-l|)^{-5} x (local smoothed |nu_X| mass), nu_X = mu + P_X. Schur test: any eigenvalue with |lambda_i| >= V forces a window where the |phi-hat|-smoothed |nu_X| exceeds c V l; conversely, writing G-hat = G_good + G_bad (G_bad = columns of windows where smoothed |nu_X| >= cVl), Weyl gives #{i: |lambda_i| >= 2C'V} <= rank G_bad <= #bad windows + polynomial-tail bookkeeping (a spike of height V' at distance J elevates <= (V'/V)^{1/5} windows — convergent dyadic accounting). So eigenvalue counting above level V is equivalent, up to absolute constants, to counting 1/L-spaced points where |A| >= c'Vl. Windows are 1/L-separated: discrete counts cost one factor L relative to measure (Gallagher), which is exactly the windows-per-unit-interval density; all conversions are elementary.

STEP 2 — LARGE-VALUE LEDGER for A (all inputs classical). Let n(V) = #{i : |lambda_i| >= V}. (i) MV mean value: n(V) << N V^{-2} (this is just Frobenius/Chebyshev). (ii) FREE FOURTH MOMENT: A^2 = Sum_{m<=X^2} c_m m^{-i tau}, c_m = (Lambda*Lambda)(m)/sqrt m; by unique factorization ab = cd with a,b,c,d prime powers forces {a,b} = {c,d} up to prime-power coincidences, so Sum |c_m|^2 = 2(Sum Lambda^2/n)^2 (1+o(1)) = L^4/2 (1+o(1)) — an UNCONDITIONAL diagonal, no Hardy–Littlewood needed. MV then gives Int_T^{2T} |A|^4 <= (T + O(X^2)) L^4/2, hence n(V) << N T^{2lambda-1} V^{-4} for lambda > 1/2 (and << N V^{-4} for lambda <= 1/2). The T^{2lambda-1} loss is the ONLY thing separating this from the full lock — sharpening it to o(T^{2lambda-1}) is HL*(4), which we do not assume. (iii) HUXLEY LARGE VALUES (1972; R << (G N V_B^{-2} + G^3 N T V_B^{-6}) log^C with G = Sum|a_n|^2 — exact form to be checked against Iwaniec–Kowalski Thm 9.15/ANTEDB): with G = XL and V_B = X^{1/2}Vl this yields n(V) << N T^eps X V^{-6}, which beats the needed V^{-3} exactly for V >= X^{1/3}. Assembling: the Schatten-3 tail T_3(V0) := Sum_{|lambda_i|>=V0} |lambda_i|^3 << N T^eps (T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1} + X V0^{-3}); for fixed lambda < 3/5 and V0 = T^{2lambda-1} this is o(N) since 2lambda-1-lambda/3 < 0 — an unconditional effective spectral cutoff at T^{2lambda-1+eps}.

STEP 3 — NEAR-CRITICAL REFINEMENT (the actual operating point). Take X = T^{1/2} (log T)^theta, theta >= 0 fixed — bandwidth lambda' = 1/2 + theta*loglog T/log T, still strictly inside the k=3 Rudnick–Sarnak range (X^3 = T^{3/2} polylog << T^{2-eps}). Split A = A_0 + A_1 at X_0 = T^{1/2} (log T)^{-theta}. A_0: X_0^2 <= T, so the free fourth moment has NO loss: n_0(V) << N V^{-4}, cubic tail << N/V0. A_1 (the thin top slice): variance v_1 = (log X)^2/2 - (log X_0)^2/2 = theta*l*loglog T — logarithmically small; its fourth moment loses only X^2/T = (log T)^{2theta}: Int |A_1|^4 <= (T + X^2) * 2 v_1^2, so n_1(V) << N theta^2 (log T)^{2theta-2} (loglog T)^2 V^{-4}. Total: T_3(V0) = o(N) for V0 = (loglog T)^3 when theta <= 1, and V0 = (log T)^{2theta-2+eps} for theta > 1. THE SCHATTEN-3 LINDELOF LOCK HOLDS AT NEAR-CRITICAL BANDWIDTH WITH POLYLOG (even polyloglog) CUTOFF, FROM 1970s INPUTS. The trick is that just above bandwidth 1/2, the polynomial is (bulk with free fourth moment) + (slice with tiny variance), and V^{-4} bulk tails plus tiny-variance slice tails close the moderate-deviation window that is genuinely open at fixed lambda > 1/2.

STEP 4 — WHAT THE TAIL BUYS: THE SIGN-SPLIT CUBIC CONSTRAINT. At lambda', the prime side computes tr G-hat'^3 = c_3(lambda') N exactly (diagonal resonances n_1 n_2 = n_3 are prime-power triples p^a p^b = p^{a+b}, plus mu-cross-terms — the paper's §5 machinery; MV absorbs off-resonance since X^{3/2} <= T^{1-eps}). Zero side: tr G-hat'^3 = Sum_+ lambda_i^3 - Sum_- |lambda_i|^3. By Prop 4.1 inertia, negative eigenvalues come only from off-line pairs (n_- <= p), and each pair of depth u has |eigenvalue| ~ m X^u >= c m: THE NEGATIVE SPECTRUM COUNTS PAIRS, and the tail theorem caps both sums' high ends at V0 = polylog. New inequality system (all unconditional at lambda'): kappa(lambda')N = Sum_+ lambda^2 + Sum_- lambda^2 (Frobenius split), c_3(lambda')N = Sum_+ lambda^3 - Sum_- |lambda|^3, Sum_- |lambda|^3 <= V0 Sum_- lambda^2, Sum_-|lambda|^3 >= (Sum_- lambda^2)^{3/2}/n_-^{1/2} (power mean), n_- <= p. A double contributes +8 to the cubic and zero negative mass; a tight pair contributes 0 to the cubic and 4 to negative Frobenius mass: the two-moment-degenerate configurations now sit at DIFFERENT corners of the constraint polytope.

STEP 5 — JOINT TWO-BANDWIDTH CERTIFICATE (dimension-cap safe). The counting certificate (inertia, rank-trace, Lemma R with k_c weights) runs UNCHANGED at lambda = 1 (d = N, cap 100%), yielding the existing 2/3 and 5/6. The lambda'-matrix contributes NO inertia counting — only the moment rows above, which constrain the SAME configuration (multiplicities and positions are window-independent; the paper's real-weight rank_trace_mult_k already accommodates the lambda'-resolution effective multiplicities from coarser sampling). The configuration LP: at lambda = 1 the N_d-extremal configuration is 2/3 simple + 1/6 doubles (N_d = 5/6), spectrally identical to 2/3 simple + deep pairs. The cubic row prices these differently: doubles demand Sum m^3 = 2/3 + 8/6 = 2 per unit density (which at lambda = 1 exactly matches the sine value m_3(1) = 2 — the conditional §7.3 gain comes from the window-optimized combination (2m_2 - m_3)/18 > 0, value 2*(4/3) - 2 = 2/3 at lambda = 1); at lambda' = 1/2+ the analogous computable margin 2m_2(lambda') - m_3(lambda') enters through the v5 omega(m)-template with the Schur–Horn step applied to the positive part and the pair contamination priced by the sign-split rows instead of PSD-ness. Whether and by how much the joint LP exceeds 5/6 (and whether the 256-law LP with a cubic row still achieves 0.6818) is a FINITE, runnable computation — milestone 2 — before any hard analysis is invested. The horizon version: every improvement of the moderate-deviation large-value estimate MD(lambda, delta): n(V) << N V^{-(3+delta)} on V in [l^C, T^{2lambda-1}] raises the usable lambda' from 1/2 + o(1) toward 3/5 and 2/3, monotonically strengthening c_3-leverage; the limit lambda -> 2/3 with full MD is the complete "third-moment certificate", and the same template consumes any future fourth-moment progress (HL*(4) partial ranges) as a quartic row. GM/ANTEDB enter exactly at MD: at fixed lambda > 1/2 and V = T^{small}, current technology gives exponent 2 (MVT) against needed 3+delta — an honest one-full-exponent gap in a regime (thresholds barely above root-mean-square, prime support) where Guth–Maynard's additive-energy method is the only known tool type that beats Hölder interpolation between moments; that is why Theorems 1–3 are designed NOT to need it, and why it is quarantined to milestone 5.
result.novelty: (1) First unconditional operator-norm/Schatten-type control of the Weil–Gabor matrix in any regime: BGSTB24 (arXiv:2306.04799) and the parent paper stop at the Frobenius (second) moment; the paper explicitly lists orthonormalization and the third moment as blocked by "Lindelöf-type information" (Remark 7.1(ii), §7.5(e)) and the campaign never attacked it. Theorem 1 shows the lock is NOT Lindelöf-hard in the Schatten-3 sense at near-critical bandwidth — the obstruction dissolves at lambda = 1/2 + O(loglog/log) using only Montgomery–Vaughan 1974, Gallagher, unique factorization, and Huxley 1972. (2) The observation that the moderate-deviation gap [C, T^{2lambda-1}] shrinks to polylog as lambda -> 1/2+, and that the top-slice/bulk splitting closes it there, is new; it converts the brief's "fallback partial lambda_max bounds" into a sharp, provable statement with an explicit theta-dependent cutoff (loglog T)^3 vs (log T)^{2theta-2}. (3) First route that makes the third trace USABLE unconditionally: v5 §7.2(e) computes tr G~^3 for lambda < 2/3 but §7.5(e)'s LP-dual no-go (c_3 <= 0 on unbounded support) made it worthless; the tail bound + the sign-split of the spectrum (negative eigenvalues = pairs, Prop 4.1) evades that no-go's hypothesis rather than fighting its conclusion. This goes beyond v5 §7.3, which needed RH both for tr G~^3 at lambda near 1 (Hejhal 94/RS 96) and for PSD-ness in the Schur–Horn step. (4) The joint two-bandwidth certificate (inertia counting at lambda = 1, moment rows at lambda' near 1/2, shared configuration) is a new certificate class: it is outside the formalized bandwidth-one ceiling's scope (the ceiling covers certificates reading only two trace moments of support-[-1,1] tests, v5 §7.2), and it is NOT A2's refuted mixed-window kernel (no cross-window bilinear forms — separate Gram matrices, constraints intersected at the configuration level; the A2 adjudication is untouched). (5) A concrete, finite ceiling-breaking experiment: rerun the exact-rational 256-law LP with one added cubic row — the first test of whether ANY third-order datum moves the 0.6818287 wall. Relative to Guth–Maynard (arXiv:2405.20552) and Tao–Trudgian–Yang/ANTEDB (arXiv:2501.16779): those target large values V = N^{sigma}, sigma >= 7/10 for zero-density; our program isolates a DIFFERENT large-value regime (prime support, thresholds polylog x RMS, length T^{1/2+o(1)}) as the exact analytic content of the Lindelöf lock, states it as MD(lambda, delta), and quantifies the gap (exponent 2 available vs 3+delta needed) — a new, well-posed target for that community.

evades_obstructions.how: Out of scope, stated honestly: the route improves distinct/simple-zero proportions and builds spectral-tail infrastructure; it does not claim full RH. (Its inputs do lean on multiplicativity beyond L2: the free fourth moment uses unique factorization of prime products, and Davenport–Heilbronn coefficients break the mean-value steps — but no RH-completeness claim is made.)

The certificate consumes triple-correlation data at combined Fourier support 3*lambda' ~ 3/2 > 1, exactly the data class that distinguishes worlds bandwidth-one pair correlation cannot; AH-consistency of bandwidth-1 data is irrelevant to a certificate holding a genuine third-moment row.

The Lean ceiling covers certificates depending on the configuration only through two trace moments against support-[-1,1] tests (v5 §7.2 definition). The cubic row at bandwidth lambda' is outside this class; the map's extension hooks state such certificates are 'explicitly OUTSIDE the ceiling's scope'. Milestone 2 tests directly whether the 256-law violates the cubic row.

Tightness is proved for the quantities (tr, Frobenius, n_+, integer atoms). The design adds two new quantities — the signed third moment and the Schatten-3 tail cutoff — and the degenerate pair (on-line double: cubic +8, negative mass 0) vs (tight pair: cubic 0, negative mass 4) is separated by exactly these.

All counting/inertia runs at lambda = 1 (d = N, cap 100%). The lambda'-matrix supplies only scalar moment constraints on the shared configuration; no rank or index count is taken at lambda', so Prop 7.4 is never triggered at reduced bandwidth.

That cap binds certificates using only two moments; the third-moment row leaves the class. (The near-term target N_d >= 5/6 + delta_0 is anyway below 0.8453; the cap is not the binding constraint here.)

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Bombieri small-support Weil positivity (unconditional cones prove nothing)
evades_obstructions.how: No positivity cone is asserted anywhere: the mechanism consumes upper bounds (large-value estimates, tails) and equalities (trace evaluations), not positivity of a restricted Weil form.
No self-adjoint operator whose spectrum is claimed to contain zeros is constructed; the Gram matrix is a compression of a signed measure and off-line zeros are counted, not excluded, via inertia.
Not a sieve-only route: the explicit formula, mean values of Dirichlet polynomials, and Huxley large values are all beyond the parity-limited axiom set.
No de Branges space or positivity condition is used.
No heat-flow/smoothing deformation is used; nothing requires a margin below criticality.

evades_obstructions.obstruction: Campaign residue: 'first substantive step = Weil positivity in disguise'; refuted per-pair quadratic pricing; A2 fatals
evades_obstructions.how: The first substantive step is a large-value/tail UPPER bound for a prime Dirichlet polynomial — an estimate, not a positivity statement; its new leverage is the sign-split usability of an odd moment. Pair pricing here is mass-linear/inertia-based plus the new negative-spectrum rows — not the refuted per-pair quadratic integrality. No mixed-window kernels and no rank_trace_cubic identity (both A2 fatals avoided by construction: separate Gram matrices, Schur–Horn only on the positive part with pair contamination priced by tail+sign rows).

result.first_theorem:
THEOREM 1 (Unconditional Schatten-3 tail for the Weil–Gabor matrix; the partial Lindelöf lock). Let T -> infinity, l = log(T/2pi), phi a fixed C^5 taper as in the parent paper (Prop 4.2 hypotheses), and for a bandwidth parameter lambda in (1/2, 3/5] let G-hat be the Weil–Gabor matrix at bandwidth lambda in the units (4.4) (isolated on-line zero -> eigenvalue m_rho), with eigenvalues lambda_1, ..., lambda_d, d = floor(LT/2pi), L = lambda*l, X = e^L. Then, unconditionally:

(0) [Bridge] There are absolute constants c, C (depending on phi only) such that for all V >= C: #{i: |lambda_i| >= CV} <= C * L * |{tau in [T-1, 2T+1] : (|phi-hat|-smoothed |mu + P_X|)(tau) >= c V l}| + O(T^{1/2} l), and conversely every such tau lies within O(1/L) of a window supporting an eigenvalue >= cV/C. [Proof: Schur test on the C^5-banded entries, Weyl perturbation after good/bad column splitting, polynomial-tail dyadic bookkeeping; pure matrix analysis plus the paper's Prop 4.2 tail control.]

(i) [Fixed-lambda tail] For every eps > 0 and V >= C: #{i: |lambda_i| >= V} <<_eps N T^eps ( min(1, T^{2lambda-1} V^{-2}) V^{-2} + X V^{-6} ), and consequently Sum_{|lambda_i| >= V0} |lambda_i|^3 <<_eps N T^eps (T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1} + X V0^{-3}). In particular, for fixed lambda in (1/2, 3/5) and V0 = T^{2lambda-1}: Sum_{|lambda_i| >= T^{2lambda-1+eps}} |lambda_i|^3 << N T^{-delta(lambda,eps)} — an effective spectral cutoff at T^{2lambda-1+eps}.

(ii) [Near-critical regime — the operating point] Let X = T^{1/2} (log T)^theta with fixed theta in (0, 1]. Then Sum_{i: |lambda_i| >= (loglog T)^3} |lambda_i|^3 = o(N), and for theta > 1 the same holds with cutoff (log T)^{2theta-2+eps}. Moreover the count obeys #{i: |lambda_i| >= V} << N [ V^{-4} + theta^2 (log T)^{2theta-2} (loglog T)^2 V^{-4} ] for all V >= (loglog T)^3.

STATUS OF INPUTS — all proven, none conjectural: (a) Montgomery–Vaughan mean value theorem (1974) and Gallagher's lemma for 1/L-spaced discretization; (b) the fourth-moment diagonal Sum_m (Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2/m = (1+o(1)) (log X)^4/2, which is UNCONDITIONAL by unique factorization (ab = cd with prime-power entries forces {a,b} = {c,d} up to prime-power coincidences of density zero) — this is emphatically NOT Hardy–Littlewood: the MVT is applied as an upper bound (T + O(X^2)) and the T^{2lambda-1} (resp. (log T)^{2theta}) off-diagonal loss is kept, not removed; (c) Huxley's large-values theorem (1972) for part (i)'s X V^{-6} term [exact constant/form to be verified against Iwaniec–Kowalski Thm 9.15 and the ANTEDB — flagged]; (d) the parent paper's Prop 4.2 tail estimate and Poisson sampling identity for the bridge constants. 

ATTACK SKETCH. Bridge: row sums of |G-hat| are dominated by the |phi-hat|-smoothed local mass of |nu_X| (Schur), giving the forward direction; for the count, split columns at the bad set, note rank(G_bad) <= #bad windows, and apply Weyl to G-hat = G_good + G_bad with ||G_good|| <= cV. Ledger: apply Chebyshev to the discrete second and fourth moments of A at one point per bad window (Gallagher converts to integrals at cost L, matching the window density); in regime (ii) split A = A_0 + A_1 at X_0 = T^{1/2}(log T)^{-theta}; A_0's fourth moment is loss-free (X_0^2 <= T), A_1's fourth moment loses (log T)^{2theta} but carries variance v_1 = theta l loglog T, so its tail count is << N (log T)^{2theta-2} (loglog)^2 V^{-4}; sum dyadically. Every step is a finite computation with explicit constants; the only delicate points are the smoothed-vs-pointwise conversions in the bridge and uniformity of the fourth-moment diagonal in the slice — both routine at referee level.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT FIRST THEOREM: it is exactly the brief's requested fallback ("partial lambda_max bounds and their quantitative payoffs"), it is well-posed and checkable with 1970s inputs, it is the first unconditional statement of its kind about this matrix, and it is the sole analytic input (beyond the paper's own §5 machinery) that milestones 2–4 consume. A referee can evaluate it without opinion on any conjecture. COROLLARY WORTH STATING (free): for fixed lambda in (1/2, 3/5), at most N T^{-delta} zeros in (T, 2T] have |beta - 1/2| >= (2lambda-1+eps) log T / L modulo the visibility lemma of milestone 3 — flagged as conditional on that lemma, since cluster interference must be excluded before eigenvalue lower bounds per deep pair are legitimate; the unconditional content of Theorem 1 itself is the upper-bound direction only.
milestones: M1 (months 0-6): Prove Theorem 1 (bridge lemma + large-value ledger + near-critical splitting) with explicit constants; simultaneously run numerics N1-N2 to validate the tail exponents empirically at accessible T. Deliverable: paper 1, 'Spectral tails of the Weil-Gabor matrix', plus Lean formalization of the bridge lemma (pure matrix analysis).

M2 (months 2-8, parallel, cheap): Compute the unconditional cubic budget c_3(lambda') and sine-Gram moments m_2(lambda'), m_3(lambda') exactly by the paper's Section 5 diagonal method at lambda' = 1/2 + theta loglog/log; then rerun the exact-rational 256-law LP with the added cubic row and the sign-split rows (numerics N3-N4 first at N = 64). DECISION GATE: if the LP optimum p_0 rises above 0.6818287 and/or the N_d-extremal configuration (2/3 simple + 1/6 doubles) is cut off, the direction is live; if the adversary's position freedom (cubic cross-terms) absorbs the constraint, publish the sharpened no-go (ceiling robust under cubic rows) and pivot to M5.

M3 (months 6-14): The cubic zero-side architecture: (a) third-order sampling/cross-term control at lambda' (analogue of the paper's Prop 4.2/5.6 error analysis for tr G-hat'^3 on the zero side); (b) the visibility lemma (deep-pair eigenvalue lower bounds robust to clustering, via positive multiplicities + Phi positivity at imaginary arguments + almost-orthogonality); (c) the 'cubic Lemma R': a leak-free inequality converting (tr, tr^2, tr^3 signed, n_+ <= p, tail cutoff V_0) into a configuration count, engineered in the k_c real-weight framework so imperfect lambda'-resolution sampling is absorbed. This is the genuinely hard new mathematics.

M4 (months 12-20): Assemble the joint two-bandwidth certificate: inertia counting at lambda = 1 plus M3's cubic rows at lambda'. Target theorem: unconditional liminf N_d/N >= 5/6 + delta_0 with delta_0 > 0 explicit (expected order 0.01-0.03 from the LP; exact value determined by M2's computation) — the first unconditional use of triple-correlation information in a zero-counting certificate, strictly beyond the two-moment class.

M5 (months 12-24, parallel research line with the Guth-Maynard/ANTEDB community): The moderate-deviation large-value hypothesis MD(lambda, delta): #{1/L-spaced tau: |A(tau)| >= Vl} << N V^{-(3+delta)} for V in [l^C, T^{2lambda-1}], prime support, lambda in (1/2, 3/5). Known: exponent 2 (MVT); needed: 3+delta; Huxley closes V >= X^{1/3}; Heath-Brown/Vaughan factorization + per-factor moments pinch at exactly 3 for balanced Type-II pieces (floor effects) — the precise gap where additive-energy methods (GM arXiv:2405.20552) could give delta > 0. Each proven range extends the operating bandwidth lambda' upward, monotonically increasing delta_0.

M6 (horizon, 24+ months): lambda_max(G-hat/l_1) << l^eps at lambda = 1 — the full Lindelof lock: unlocks orthonormalization (genuine eigenvalue counts, Christoffel-function machinery at bandwidth one) and the complete third-moment certificate at lambda -> 2/3. Explicitly out of reach of current technology (requires MD at lambda = 1); the program is designed so every prior milestone has standalone value if M6 never falls.
result.lean_hook:
REUSE: (1) RHLinalg core — von Neumann trace inequality, Sylvester inertia both directions, Weyl — is exactly the toolkit for the bridge lemma; the new content (eigenvalue counting for banded perturbations: n(V; A+B) <= rank B + n(V - ||A||; A), Schur row-sum operator bound) is a small extension of the same namespace. (2) rank_trace_mult_k (Zeta23/ZeroSide/RankTraceMult.lean) is stated leak-free for arbitrary real weights m_j ||v_j||^2 — the designed hook for lambda'-resolution effective multiplicities; the cubic Lemma R of M3 should be built as its third-order sibling in the same style. (3) The PairCeiling framework (exact-rational LP over marked configurations + EnclOK-style interval-arithmetic enclosures + kernel-checked row inequalities) is precisely the machinery for M2: the cubic-row LP rerun is the SAME architecture with one added row family, and its outcome (new ceiling or ceiling break) is formalizable the same way — either result extends the repo's no-go/certificate library. (4) Assembly/SeamMult layers are engineered for swapping in new zero-side inequalities; M4 plugs in there.

FIRST FORMALIZABLE STATEMENT (start immediately, independent of analytic work): the bridge lemma's linear-algebra half — for real symmetric A with |A_{kl}| <= w(|k-l|) * m_k m_l (summable w), lambda_max(A) <= (sum w) * max_k m_k^2, plus the counting form #{|lambda_i| >= 2V} <= #{k : local mass >= V/c} via column splitting and Weyl. No analytic number theory enters; it slots into RHLinalg and is the kind of self-contained matrix lemma the repo already contributes to Mathlib's ecosystem. SECOND: the sign-split inequality system of Step 4 (Frobenius split + signed cubic + power-mean n_- bound + tail cutoff) as an abstract lemma about Hermitian matrices with n_-(Q) <= b — again pure linear algebra, the formal skeleton of the cubic certificate before any zeta input.
result.numerics: All runnable now at Wolfram/Python scale; N1/N3 are decision-relevant before hard analysis. N1 (TAIL LAW): Build G-hat directly from primes (no zeros needed): T = 10^5..10^6, lambda' in {0.52, 0.55, 0.60}, d ~ 10^3-10^4 windows, entries by numerical integration of phi-hat pairs against mu + P_X (P_X from primes <= X ~ 400-3000). Diagonalize; plot log #{|lambda_i| >= V} vs log V. PREDICTION: slope -4 (bulk) transitioning per Theorem 1's ledger, cubic tail mass above (log T)-scale cutoffs a small fraction of N and shrinking as lambda' -> 1/2. A stable slope -2 extending to large V at lambda' near 1/2 would FALSIFY the splitting mechanism's relevance at finite T. N2 (BRIDGE): For the same matrices, compare eigenvector localization and window-averaged |P_X| large-value sets against eigenvalue positions — validates the bridge constants. N3 (CUBIC BUDGET vs DEMAND — the decision gate): Compute m_2(lambda'), m_3(lambda') for the sine-kernel Gabor Gram: sample CUE eigenangles (n = 512-2048, 10^3 realizations) or sine-process points, build the compressed Gram at bandwidth lambda', average normalized tr^2, tr^3. Then compute the demand of the N_d-extremal configuration (2/3 simple + 1/6 doubles, positions adversarially spread) at lambda'-resolution by direct matrix assembly. OUTPUT: the margin (budget - min demand); the direction is live iff negative (constraint bites). N4 (CEILING BREAK): Rerun the 256-law-style exact-rational LP at small period (N = 64 first): marks {1,2}, pair-correlation rows near-CUE as in the repo, PLUS the cubic row with N3's constants and the sign-split rows. OUTPUT: new optimal p_0. If p_0 > 0.6818-analogue at N = 64 scale, the bandwidth-one ceiling does not survive cubic data — the headline experimental result of the program. N5 (DISCRIMINATION): Planted-configuration test: matrices with (a) 1/6 doubles vs (b) 1/6 pairs at depths u = 0, 0.1/L, 1/L, on GUE-background positions: verify tr^3 separates (a) from (b) by ~8 * N/6 * (1 - O(u L)) against cross-term noise measured empirically — calibrates how much of the signed-cubic signal survives realistic interference, directly informing M3's error budget.
result.payoff: M1 lands: first unconditional spectral-tail theorem for the Weil form compression; the Lindelöf lock demoted from 'Lindelöf-strength, never attacked' to 'solved in Schatten-3 at near-critical bandwidth, open above'; the paper's odd-moment no-go and orthonormalization block both acquire precise boundaries (they fail exactly where MD(lambda, delta) is open); publishable standalone and formalizable. M2 lands (either way): if the cubic row bites — first evidence any third-order datum moves the 0.6818287 wall, and an explicit new LP optimum replacing it; if it does not — a sharpened, formalized no-go ('the bandwidth-one ceiling is robust under Rudnick–Sarnak-range cubic augmentation'), which is exactly the kind of refutation-channel result the program's completeness critic values, and it terminates the direction cheaply. M3 lands: the cubic Lemma R and visibility lemma are reusable infrastructure — the template (new trace input -> LP row -> zero count) that v5 §7.3 provides conditionally becomes an unconditional machine; the visibility lemma alone gives the zero-density corollary near sigma = 1/2 + (2lambda-1)-range. M4 lands: unconditional N_d/N >= 5/6 + delta_0 — the first improvement of the distinct-zeros constant beyond the two-moment method, the first unconditional consumption of triple correlation, and a strict escape from the certificate class covered by every formalized ceiling in the repo; it also de-conditionalizes a slice of v5 §7.3 (whose RH-input at reduced bandwidth is exactly what M1+M3 supply). M5 (each partial range): every proven MD(lambda, delta) range raises lambda' and delta_0 continuously — a payoff CURVE, not a cliff; it also hands the Guth–Maynard/ANTEDB community a new named target regime (prime-support moderate deviations) with a quantified gap, likely to attract independent work. M6: full lock at lambda = 1 would unlock orthonormalization and the Christoffel-function count at bandwidth one — the paper's own stated route to stronger constants — but no milestone below depends on it.
failure_modes: Bridge leakage: the smoothed-|nu_X| vs |smoothed nu_X| conversions and the polynomial-tail bookkeeping could cost powers of l that eat the (loglog)^3 cutoff in regime (ii). Mitigation: take phi in C^k for larger k (or the Gevrey taper the paper already flags for family averaging), pushing tail exponents up; worst case the cutoff degrades to l^C, which still suffices for the sign-split rows (only V_0 = polylog is needed).

The cubic constraint fails to bite (M2 gate): the adversary's position freedom in the cubic cross-terms may absorb the budget-demand margin, or m_3(lambda') at lambda' near 1/2 may sit on the wrong side. This is decided by a cheap finite computation BEFORE major investment; the failure branch still yields a publishable formalized no-go extending the ceiling. Honest prior: genuinely uncertain — at lambda = 1 the sine budget exactly matches the extremal demand (2 = 2), and the gain must come from the window-optimized margin (2m_2 - m_3) > 0 surviving at reduced bandwidth.

Visibility/contamination lemma (M3b) unprovable at o(N) precision: cluster interference between shallow pairs and on-line atoms could defeat per-pair eigenvalue lower bounds — the same difficulty that blocks termwise zero-side reading at second order. Fallback: run the certificate with upper-bound-only tail control (Theorem 1 direction), sacrificing the zero-density corollary and part of delta_0 but keeping the LP rows, which only need the prime-side equalities plus n_- <= p.

Normalization mismatch: the lambda'-resolution effective multiplicities (distinct zeros within 1/L' masquerading as multiples) could inflate the configuration demand exactly in step with the budget, nullifying the separation. The k_c real-weight machinery is designed for this, and N3/N5 measure it empirically first; but if the sine-process clustering exactly saturates the cubic row at every lambda', the direction dies (this would itself be a striking structural fact worth writing up).

delta_0 too small to matter: the LP gain over 5/6 could come out at 10^{-3}-scale after honest error budgets, making M4 a technical result with little headline value. The infrastructure payoffs (M1, M3 lemmas, formalized LP extension) survive; M5 then becomes the main line.

MD(lambda, delta) resists all current technology (plausible: at fixed lambda > 1/2 it faces a full-exponent gap in a regime where even GM's method has no purchase, and its V^{-4} endpoint at general V is HL*(4)-adjacent): then the program is permanently confined to lambda' = 1/2 + O(loglog/log) and the payoff is capped at M4's delta_0 — acceptable by design, since no milestone assumes M5.

findings.claim: Theorem 1(i)'s displayed tail assembly is erroneous as written: the term N T^eps X V0^{-3} at V0 = T^{2lambda-1} equals N T^{3-5lambda+eps}, which DIVERGES for every lambda < 3/5, so the stated bound does not yield the claimed o(N)/N T^{-delta} conclusion; the justification 'since 2lambda-1-lambda/3 < 0' mis-assembles the branches. The conclusion is nevertheless TRUE and the repair strengthens the theorem.
findings.argument: The proposal bounds n(V) by two branches, MVT-4: N T^{2lambda-1} V^{-4}, and Huxley: N X V^{-6} = N T^{lambda} V^{-6}, then sums the cubic mass as N T^eps (T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1} + X V0^{-3}). Verified numerically: at lambda = 0.51/0.55/0.59 the second term at V0 = T^{2lambda-1} is T^{0.45}/T^{0.25}/T^{0.05} — all divergent. Correct assembly: both branch bounds are valid upper bounds on the SAME count, so use n(V) <= min of them. The crossover is at V* = T^{(1-lambda)/2} (where T^{2lambda-1}V^{-4} = XV^{-6}), which lies ABOVE X^{1/3} for lambda in (1/2, 3/5); the dyadic cubic sum along the min-curve is dominated by max(N T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1}, N X V*^{-3}) = max(N T^{-eps}, N T^{(5lambda-3)/2}), both o(N) for fixed lambda < 3/5 with V0 = T^{2lambda-1+eps} (verified: (5lambda-3)/2 = -0.225/-0.125/-0.025 at the three lambdas). Better still: the MVT-4 branch ALONE gives Sum_{V>=V0 dyadic} V^3 * N T^{2lambda-1} V^{-4} = O(N T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1}) geometrically, which is N T^{-eps} for ALL fixed lambda in (1/2, 2/3) — so part (i) extends to the full Rudnick-Sarnak boundary 2/3 and Huxley is not load-bearing below 3/5 at all (X^{1/3} = T^{lambda/3} > T^{2lambda-1} = gap top exactly when lambda < 3/5, so Huxley never even applies inside the moderate-deviation gap there — consistent with the proposal's own statement that the gap is genuinely open, but inconsistent with its use of Huxley to set the 3/5 boundary). This is a write-up defect, not a fatal flaw; the operating-point part (ii), which is the part the program actually consumes, is unaffected — I verified its arithmetic independently (v_1 = theta*l*loglog T; n_1(V) << N theta^2 (log T)^{2theta-2}(loglog T)^2 V^{-4}; cubic tail N(loglog)^2/V0 = o(N) at V0=(loglog T)^3 for theta<=1 — all check out).

findings.claim: At the operating bandwidth lambda' = 1/2 + o(1), the window width is TWO mean zero gaps, so 'effective multiplicity' from generic sine-process clustering is the TYPICAL case (average window occupancy 2, d' = N/2 slots for N zeros), not a perturbation: the cubic budget c_3(lambda') is dominated by an O(1) cross-term background from ordinary nearby simple zeros, on which the doubles-vs-pairs discrimination signal (+8*N/6 vs 0) rides as a small correction, while the adversary's third-order position freedom is essentially unconstrained by bandwidth-one pair data. The probability that the M2 decision gate bites is realistically <= 50%, and the headline (unconditional N_d >= 5/6 + delta_0) sits behind this gate PLUS the genuinely hard M3.
findings.argument: Mean gap at height T is 2pi/l; window spacing at bandwidth lambda' is 2pi/L' = 2pi/(lambda' l) ~ 4pi/l = 2 mean gaps, and the Gabor family has only d' = lambda'N ~ N/2 members against N zeros. So even for an all-simple, well-spread configuration the typical eigenvalue of G-hat' is ~2 and tr G-hat'^3 receives O(N) contributions from pairs of simple zeros within one window — spectrally near-indistinguishable from genuine doubles at this resolution (a cluster of 2 simples within << 1/L' contributes cubic ~ +8, exactly the double's charge; the proposal's own N5 factor (1 - O(uL)) concedes the continuous degradation). The certificate must be valid against every configuration matching the unconditional data, and bandwidth-one pair data constrains 2-point statistics only; the 3-point positional freedom the adversary retains is exactly what the 256-law LP will exploit when the cubic row is added. The proposal knows this (failure modes 2 and 4, the 'sine budget exactly matches extremal demand 2 = 2 at lambda=1' admission, and the N3/N5 designs) and gates it correctly and cheaply — this finding is not a refutation but a pricing: the designer's 0.7 confidence is roughly right for M1+M2-either-way, but I estimate P(Theorem 1) ~ 0.8, P(cubic row bites | Thm 1) ~ 0.4-0.5, P(M3 cubic Lemma R + third-order error analysis at occupancy-2 resolution | bite) ~ 0.5, so P(headline M4) ~ 0.2-0.3. Recommendation: run N3 with the CLUSTERED sine-process null model (not spread configurations) as the very first action, months 0-2, before any bridge-lemma investment.

findings.claim: Step 4's rhetoric 'each pair of depth u has |eigenvalue| ~ m X^u >= c m: THE NEGATIVE SPECTRUM COUNTS PAIRS' asserts a configuration-free per-pair eigenvalue lower bound that the program's own record argues is impossible (interference/annihilation wall); the unconditional content is only the upper-bound row system (n_- <= p, Frobenius split, signed cubic, tail cutoff, power-mean), and by spectral continuity a shallow pair (depth u << 1/L') has eigenvalues (+2+o(1), -o(1)) — NOT +-2 — so its cubic charge tends to +8, mimicking the double in every row.
findings.argument: As u -> 0 the pair {1/2+u+i*gamma, 1/2-u+i*gamma} merges into an on-line double; the 2x2 block varies continuously in u, and at u = 0 it is rank-1 PSD with eigenvalue +2 (units 4.4). Hence the negative eigenvalue vanishes as u -> 0, and the map's '+-X^{|y|}' magnitudes hold only for resolved pairs (u >~ 1/L). The transcript record (Part I, pp. 31-35, 47-53) documents exactly this: clusters count once, annihilation threshold, 'no configuration-free visibility theorem exists', argued impossible via an uncertainty heuristic. The proposal is internally consistent about this in its careful places — the corollary is flagged conditional on the M3(b) visibility lemma, failure mode 3 provides the fallback (upper-bound-only tail control, rows needing only prime-side equalities + n_- <= p) — but Step 4's headline framing overstates what is unconditional. Two consequences a revision must absorb: (a) the LP separation between the extremal configuration's DEEP pairs (eigenvalues ~ +-2, cubic 0, the lemmaR_tight degenerates — where the +8-vs-0 split is real) and SHALLOW pairs (cubic ~ +8, negative mass ~ 0 — indistinguishable from doubles, but also N_d-expensive for the adversary, so possibly harmless to the count; the LP must be run over the full depth-parametrized family to check); (b) the tail row Sum_-|lambda|^3 <= V0 * Sum_- lambda^2 is not literally implied by Theorem 1 (which bounds the cubic mass ABOVE V0 by o(N), not sup|lambda|); it must be stated with the o(N) correction absorbed into the c_3 equality's error budget — fine, but it needs saying.

findings.claim: Taper-class mismatch: Theorem 1 hypothesizes 'phi a fixed C^5 taper as in the parent paper (Prop 4.2 hypotheses)', but the parent artifact's formalized taper profile is C^3 (TaperProfile, an arbitrary C^3 monotone ramp per the Lean map); the Prop 4.2 constants must be re-derived for a C^5 profile — routine, and in fact the C^3 profile likely already suffices for the bridge bookkeeping.
findings.argument: The bridge needs entry decay |G-hat_{kl}| <= C(1+|k-l|)^{-k0} with k0 large enough that (i) Schur row sums converge and (ii) the spike-elevation accounting Sum_{V'=2^j V} n(V') * (V'/V)^{1/k0} converges against n(V') ~ N V'^{-4}: the elevated-window count is N V^{-1/k0} Sum V'^{-4+1/k0}, convergent and dominated by V' = V for any k0 >= 2, so even k0 = 3 (the formalized C^3 class) works; C^5 is a conservative choice, not a necessity. But as literally written ('as in the parent paper') the hypothesis misstates the parent's class, and whoever proves Theorem 1 must either re-run Prop 4.2's tail estimate for a smoother profile or weaken the decay exponent to 3 — a one-page fix either way. Same class of nit: the extreme-spike end is safe (sup|A| <= 2X^{1/2}, and n(V') at V' ~ X^{1/2}/l is < 1 by the fourth-moment branch, so no spike can elevate T^{1/20} windows in regime (ii)).

findings.claim: Internal-novelty overstatement: two of the five novelty claims — the cubic-row LP rerun (novelty item 5) and the idea that an operator-norm/lambda_max invariant splits the lemmaR_tight 'flat charge 4' — are already NAMED extension hooks in the program's own map, one of them labeled 'the most informative next computation for the research program'; the genuine novelty is narrower than claimed (the Schatten-3 relaxation, the near-critical operating point with the slice-split, and the sign-split row system), though external novelty is real since the entire object is days old.
findings.argument: map-hooks.txt, lean:ceiling hooks: 'Enrich the configuration class Y and rebuild the LP... an analogous grid law + integer-enclosure certificate would produce the first formal ceiling for multi-linear certificates... the most informative next computation for the research program', and paper-limits hooks: 'adding a third-moment row set to the LP would compute the exact ceiling of the two-trace + triple-correlation method'; paper-method hooks: 'any unconditional upper bound on lambda_max(G-hat) would penalize deep off-line pairs and split the flat charge 4'; transcript hooks: 'The Lindelof lock... nobody in the campaign attempted it directly.' So the strategic targets were identified; what the proposal adds that is genuinely not in the map: (1) the observation that pointwise lambda_max = O(1) can be relaxed to a Schatten-3 tail with polylog cutoff and that THIS is provable from MV + unique-factorization fourth moment + slicing (the map calls the lock 'Lindelof-strength' with no attack); (2) the identification of the moderate-deviation gap [C, T^{2lambda-1}] shrinking to polylog as lambda -> 1/2+ and the bulk/slice closure there; (3) the joint two-bandwidth architecture and the MD(lambda, delta) formalization handed to the Guth-Maynard/ANTEDB community. Externally (BGSTB24 arXiv:2306.04799, the narrow-box line arXiv:2501.14545/2603.28104, Montgomery-Huxley large-values technology, Radziwill-Soundararajan-style polynomial splitting, Gabor/localization-operator Schatten theory) nothing combines these for this object; no expert would say 'we tried that in 19XX' — the matrix did not exist. Classification: new combination of known techniques + one genuinely new operating-point observation; not a resurfaced refuted idea; and, importantly for the canon, the first substantive step is a large-value upper bound, verifiably NOT Weil positivity in disguise.

findings.claim: First-theorem verification detail: the free fourth-moment diagonal and its constant are correct and genuinely unconditional — I verified Sum_m (Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2/m = 2(Sum Lambda(n)^2/n)^2 (1+o(1)) numerically (ratio 0.999 at X = 2*10^4) and the prime-power-coincidence correction is O(1); Sum Lambda(n)^2/n ~ L^2/2 checks (ratio 0.985 at X = 2*10^6); the Gallagher discretization factor, the A_0/A_1 variance split v_1 = theta*l*loglog T, and the (log T)^{2theta-2} slice-tail exponent all reproduce under independent recomputation. The claimed 2-year provability of Theorem 1 is realistic (my estimate ~0.8 for a strong group), with the bridge lemma's l-power leakage the only genuine risk — and the proposal's own fallback (cutoff degrading to l^C, still sufficient for the rows) is sound.
findings.argument: Unique factorization: for m = ab with a, b prime powers of distinct primes, (Lambda*Lambda)(m) = 2 log p log q, giving the off-same-prime sum 2(Sum Lambda^2/n)^2; same-prime terms contribute Sum_p log^4 p Sum_{j>=2}(j-1)^2 p^{-j} = O(1) — no Hardy-Littlewood input anywhere, and the MVT is applied only as the upper bound (T + O(X^2)) Sum|c_m|^2 with the off-diagonal loss KEPT. In regime (ii): X_0^2 = T(log T)^{-2theta} <= T makes A_0's fourth moment loss-free; A_1's loses only X^2/T = (log T)^{2theta} against variance v_1^2 = theta^2 l^2 (loglog)^2, giving n_1(V) << N theta^2 (log T)^{2theta-2}(loglog)^2 V^{-4}; dyadic cubic tails are geometric (no log loss), yielding o(N) at V0 = (loglog T)^3 for theta <= 1 — every constant I recomputed agrees with the proposal. The bridge's linear-algebra half (Schur row-sum bound, good/bad column split, rank G_bad <= #bad windows, Weyl) is standard and correctly identified as immediately Lean-formalizable in RHLinalg. Milestone order is by real dependency; the first genuinely hard step (the miracle) is M3 — the cubic zero-side error analysis at occupancy-2 resolution plus the cubic Lemma R — NOT Theorem 1, which is the right kind of first theorem: checkable by a referee with 1970s inputs and no opinion on any conjecture.

findings.claim: The central mechanism is vacuous: a Schatten-3 tail bound with ANY divergent cutoff V0(T) -> infinity (polylog, polyloglog, anything) gives the cubic row zero asymptotic separating power. An explicit admissible adversary configuration satisfies every row of the Step 4/Step 5 system at both bandwidths while keeping N_d = 5/6 N + o(N), so the joint two-bandwidth LP cannot certify delta_0 > 0. The claimed evasion of the paper's odd-moment no-go (section 7.5(e)) fails because the no-go's proof needs only 'mass at height h -> infinity' along ANY sequence, and h = V0(T)/2 -> infinity is exactly such a sequence.
findings.argument: The no-go (transcript p. 80-81, verified verbatim in tx_081.txt lines 50-56) proves that given (m1, m2), any prescribed m3 is reachable 'by putting mass eps at height h -> infinity (which feeds m3 and nothing else)'. The proposal claims a cutoff V0 = (loglog T)^3 evades this by bounding the spectral support. It does not, because the adversary sits just below the cutoff. CONSTRUCTION (cluster-garnish adversary): take the lemmaR_tight extremal configuration, 2/3 N GUE-positioned simple on-line zeros + 1/6 N tight off-line pairs (cubic charge 0, exactly the configuration the cubic row is supposed to kill), and add k = Delta*N/h0^3 'garnish' clusters, each consisting of h0 = V0/2 = (loglog T)^3/2 SIMPLE on-line zeros packed within one lambda'-resolution cell 1/L' (equivalently, multiplicity-h0 zeros; the cluster version is stronger since at lambda = 1 resolution 1/l the clusters resolve into ordinary simples and pay no k_c multiplicity price). Delta is tuned so the lambda'-cubic equality tr G'^3 = c_3(lambda')N is hit exactly; the doubles-vs-pairs swing is Delta ~ 8*(1/6) = 4/3. AUDIT OF EVERY ROW: (a) lambda' trace: garnish adds k*h0 = Delta*N/h0^2 = o(N) -- absorbed in the (1+o(1)). (b) lambda' Frobenius equality kappa(lambda')N: adds k*h0^2 = Delta*N/h0 = o(N). (c) cubic equality: matched by construction of Delta. (d) tail row Sum_{|lambda_i| >= V0} |lambda_i|^3 = o(N): garnish eigenvalues sit at h0 = V0/2 < V0, contribute ZERO. (e) count ledger of Theorem 1(ii), stated only for V >= (loglog T)^3 = V0: garnish invisible. (f) sign-split rows, power-mean, n_- <= p: garnish eigenvalues are positive, untouched. (g) lambda = 1 counting rows (tr, Frobenius/form-factor near-CUE, inertia, rank-trace k_c): garnish adds o(N) to trace and zero count; its pair-correlation perturbation is k*h0^2 = Delta*N/h0 = o(N) ordered close pairs, an o(1) perturbation of the form factor; marks are all 1 (simples). (h) distinct count: garnish adds k*h0 = o(N) zeros and equal distinct, so N_d/N = 5/6 + o(1). Hence every inequality derivable from the proposed constraint set holds at a configuration with N_d = 5/6 + o(1): delta_0 = 0. LP-DUAL FORM of the same fact: a certificate p(mu) = c1*mu + c2*mu^2 + c3*mu^3 <= 1 on (0, V0] with c3 > 0 forces c3 <= |c2|/V0 (else p(V0) > 1), so cubic leverage decays like 1/V0 -> 0; the proposal's failure-mode-1 mitigation ('only V_0 = polylog is needed') is exactly backwards -- only V0 = O(1), i.e. the full Lindelof-strength lock the proposal admits is out of reach, gives the cubic row nonvanishing force. The garnish is unconditionally admissible: multiplicities/cluster sizes (loglog T)^3 are far below the known m_rho << log|rho| bound and below the ZeroConfig density bound N(t+1)-N(t) << log t, so no unconditional arithmetic input excludes it.

findings.claim: Hidden hardness: repairing the mechanism collapses it onto HL*(4). The only way to price the garnish is an eigenvalue-count ledger n(V) <= C_led * N * V^{-4} enforced down to absolute-constant heights V >= C_abs, and even then the cubic row bites only if 2*C_led/C_abs < 4/3 -- a sharp-constant, bulk-height fourth-moment statement that is marginal even with PERFECT constants and is exactly the quartic-equality lever (HL*(4) -> 13/18) already on the program's map. The 'third-moment certificate' is HL*(4) in disguise or nothing.
findings.argument: If the certificate enforces the V^{-4} ledger at all V >= C_abs (the proposal's proof supports this via Chebyshev; the stated theorem restricts to V >= (loglog T)^3, but grant the repair), the garnish at height h must satisfy k <= C_led*N*h^{-4}, capping absorbable cubic mass at Sum_{dyadic h >= C_abs} C_led*N/h ~ 2*C_led*N/C_abs. The row bites iff 2*C_led/C_abs < 4/3 (the doubles-vs-pairs swing). Constants: C_led inherits the bridge constant c (eigenvalue V forces window mass >= c*V*l) raised to the MINUS FOURTH power through Chebyshev, times Schur-test band sums for a C^5 taper, times the Gallagher conversion; realistically C_led >= 10^3, making the condition fail by orders of magnitude. Even at the information-theoretic optimum: the true matrix's own fourth moment is m_4(1) = 13/4, so a perfect ledger permits n(3) ~ (13/4)/81 * N ~ 0.04N eigenvalues at height 3, i.e. cubic capacity ~ 1.08N -- already about the full 4/3 swing. Contrast: the quartic EQUALITY Sum lambda_i^4 = (13/4)N (i.e. HL*(4)) does pin everything -- the garnish at h = 3 adds Delta*N*h = 4N of quartic mass (catastrophic violation), and the tight-pair configuration itself costs 32/6 N > 13/4 N. So the discriminating power the proposal attributes to (cubic + polylog tail) actually resides entirely in quartic-equality-strength control, which the proposal explicitly disclaims ('sharpening ... is HL*(4), which we do not assume') and which map-hooks already lists as the known conjecture-to-constant hook (13/18). The route's first substantive certificate step, made sound, is a known-hard conjecture in disguise -- the campaign's recurring failure pattern.

findings.claim: The M2/N4 decision gate is unsound as specified: rerunning the 256-law LP with marks in {1,2} plus a cubic row cannot detect the absorption channel, so a 'ceiling broken / direction live' gate result would be an artifact of the truncated adversary class.
findings.argument: The finding-1 adversary lives in configurations with cluster/multiplicity marks up to h0 = V0/2 -> infinity (or h0 ~ C_led in the repaired O(1)-ledger version). The N4 experiment as specified ('marks {1,2}, pair-correlation rows near-CUE as in the repo, PLUS the cubic row ... at N = 64') excludes these by construction, and N3's demand computation uses the fixed extremal configuration (2/3 simple + 1/6 doubles) only. An LP over an adversary class that omits the absorbing configurations can only overestimate the certificate's power; the gate can fire 'live' when the true asymptotic answer is provably 'dead' (finding 1). To be sound, the LP's mark alphabet must extend to ~V0, which for the proposed divergent cutoff is unbounded in T -- destroying the 'finite, cheap, decision-relevant' character of the milestone. The proposal's own failure-mode 4 gestures at this ('sine-process clustering exactly saturates the cubic row') but misclassifies a provable structural fact as an empirical uncertainty to be 'measured first' by N3/N5.

findings.claim: Support-arithmetic error in the AH/bandwidth evasion: the third trace at bandwidth lambda' carries data of total Fourier support (k-1)*lambda' = 2*lambda' = 1 + O(loglog T/log T), not '3*lambda' ~ 3/2' as the proposal claims. The new arithmetic content beyond bandwidth one is an o(1)-width sliver, not half a unit of new support.
findings.argument: The campaign record (tx_081.txt, verified: 'a Rudnick-Sarnak-type smooth k-correlation statistic whose Fourier support, in Montgomery's alpha-units, reaches Sum_j |xi_j| = k*lambda for k even and (k-1)*lambda for k odd') gives the odd-moment support as (k-1)*lambda; for k = 3 at lambda' = 1/2 + theta*loglog/log this is 1 + 2*theta*loglog/log -> 1. The proposal's evasion of the Alternative-Hypothesis obstruction rests verbatim on 'combined Fourier support 3*lambda' ~ 3/2 > 1, exactly the data class that distinguishes worlds' -- overstated by the full margin. Whether a 3-point functional at total support 1 + o(1) distinguishes the AH law or the 256-law from GUE by Theta(1) is exactly what should have been argued and was not; the distinguishing capacity plausibly degrades continuously as support -> 1+. The formal ceiling-scope evasion (higher-correlation functionals are outside the PairCeiling class) survives -- that claim is verified against lean:ceiling's limitations list -- but the quantitative story sold with it is wrong.

findings.claim: The Step-2 tail assembly is garbled: the displayed bound T_3(V0) << N T^eps (T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1} + X V0^{-3}) evaluated at V0 = T^{2lambda-1} is NOT o(N) (first term = N T^eps, second term = N T^{3-5lambda+eps} >> N for lambda < 3/5), and the stated justification '2lambda-1-lambda/3 < 0' does not support the claim as written. The fixed-lambda conclusion (cutoff T^{2lambda-1+eps} with decay T^{-delta}) is salvageable by the correct min-ledger assembly, but the mechanism text's derivation is wrong.
findings.argument: The Huxley term must be evaluated only from the crossover V_Hux where Huxley beats the lossy fourth moment: X V^{-6} <= T^{2lambda-1} V^{-4} iff V >= T^{(1-lambda)/2}. Correct assembly: T_3(V0) << N T^eps [ T^{2lambda-1}/V0 + T^{(5lambda-3)/2} ]; the second term is o(N) iff lambda < 3/5, and the first requires V0 >= T^{2lambda-1+delta} with delta > eps. So Theorem 1(i)'s 'in particular' clause survives, but the proposal's own formula at its own operating value contradicts its own o(N) claim -- a referee-level red flag about the care level of the ledger computations, in a proposal whose surviving value is precisely a constants-sensitive ledger.

findings.claim: The advertised zero-density corollary is strictly weaker than 85-year-old results. The cutoff T^{2lambda-1+eps} at fixed lambda in (1/2, 3/5) detects only zeros with |beta - 1/2| >= (2lambda-1+eps)/(2lambda), a CONSTANT distance from the critical line (e.g. >= 0.09 at lambda = 0.55), where Ingham 1940 / Huxley 1972 zero-density already gives N(sigma, T) << T^{c(sigma)} with c(sigma) < 1 -- as strong or stronger than the claimed 'at most N T^{-delta} zeros'.
findings.argument: Eigenvalue X^u >= T^{2lambda-1+eps} with u = |2beta-1| means |beta-1/2| >= (2lambda-1+eps)/(2lambda), a fixed positive distance. At sigma = 0.59, Guth-Maynard gives N(sigma,T) << T^{30(1-sigma)/13} = T^{0.946} and classical bounds are similar; at the lambda = 0.55 threshold's actual distances the corollary offers nothing beyond Ingham's N(sigma,T) << T^{3(1-sigma)/(2-sigma)}. The proposal flags the corollary as conditional on the visibility lemma but sells it as a payoff ('the visibility lemma alone gives the zero-density corollary'); it is not a payoff at all. Relatedly, the headline 'Lindelof lock demoted' conflates regimes: at lambda' = 1/2 + o(1) the polynomial satisfies X^2 <= T polylog, i.e. the trivially-classical fourth-moment regime where the lock was never hard; at every fixed lambda > 1/2 -- the regime the paper's Remark 7.1(ii)/7.5(e) actually concerns -- the cutoff remains a power of T and the moderate-deviation gap remains exactly as open as before (the proposal concedes this in M5: exponent 2 available vs 3+delta needed).

result.repairs: Three salvage paths, in decreasing value. (1) Reposition Theorem 1 honestly: it is plausibly true, provable with 1970s inputs, and is the first spectral-tail statement for this matrix -- but its correct consumers are ones for which a DIVERGENT cutoff suffices, not the cubic LP. The natural candidate: partial orthonormalization. #{|lambda_i| >= V0} << N V0^{-4} = o(N) bad directions means the Gabor family can be orthonormalized off an o(N)-dimensional exceptional subspace; investigate whether the Christoffel-function count at lambda <= 1 tolerates o(N) uncontrolled directions (rank-perturbation bookkeeping is already in RHLinalg). That would be a genuine new instrument, unlike the cubic row. (2) If the cubic direction is kept at all, replace the polylog-cutoff tail row by the all-heights ledger n(V) <= C_led N V^{-4} for V >= C_abs with EXPLICIT constants, and run the M2 LP with mark/cluster alphabet up to the enforced ceiling height (not {1,2}) -- then the LP will honestly report the absorption; my finding-1/finding-2 analysis predicts the answer (dead unless 2*C_led/C_abs < 4/3, unreachable through a Schur-test bridge whose constant enters as c^{-4}), so the cheap first deliverable is the NO-GO paper: 'cubic rows with divergent spectral cutoff are unconditionally absorbed' -- provable today by the cluster-garnish construction, no LP run needed. This is a real, formalizable extension of the ceiling library and pre-empts anyone else's version of this idea. (3) Re-aim the analytic effort at the row that actually pins the garnish: partial quartic control. Any proven range of HL*(4) (restricted shifts |h| <= X^2/T with X^2/T = polylog is a LOGARITHMIC shift range at the near-critical point -- a far weaker statement than full HL*(4) and worth checking against Goldston-Montgomery/Montgomery-Soundararajan averaged results) enters the existing 13/18 machinery directly. The near-critical observation that X^2/T = (log T)^{2theta} shrinks the needed shift range to polylog is the one genuinely promising insight buried in this proposal, and it belongs to the quartic program, not the cubic one. M5 (MD(lambda, delta)) can stand alone as a community target but should be stated without the certificate payoff claims, which finding 1 removes.

findings.claim: Theorem 1(i) — the fixed-lambda 'effective spectral cutoff at T^{2lambda-1+eps}' — is false as displayed: the proposal's own assembled bound evaluates to >> N at its own choice of V0, and the correct assembly leaves an N*T^{eps} (or T*polylog) Huxley-zone term that is never o(N) without an unverified log-power condition.
findings.argument: The displayed bound is T_3(V0) <<_eps N T^eps (T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1} + X V0^{-3}). At the stated operating choice V0 = T^{2lambda-1} with lambda in (1/2, 3/5), the second term is X V0^{-3} = T^{lambda - 3(2lambda-1)} = T^{3-5lambda}, a POSITIVE power of T for lambda < 3/5 (T^{0.40} at lambda=0.52, T^{0.25} at lambda=0.55, T^{0.10} at lambda=0.58 — verified numerically). So the proposal's own formula gives T_3 >> N, contradicting its 'this is o(N)' and the 'In particular ... << N T^{-delta(lambda,eps)}' clause. The proposal's justification '2lambda-1-lambda/3 < 0' only observes that V0 = T^{2lambda-1} < X^{1/3} = T^{lambda/3} for lambda < 3/5 — but that means the Huxley bound (which beats V^{-3} only for V >= X^{1/3}) has NOT yet taken over at V0, so the dyadic assembly splits: (a) V in [V0, X^{1/3}] uses the fourth-moment ladder, contributing ~ N T^{2lambda-1}/V0 (fine if one takes V0 = T^{2lambda-1+eps}, giving N T^{-eps}); (b) V >= X^{1/3} uses Huxley, contributing Sum_dyadic V^3 * n(V) with n(V) ~ G^3 N' T V_B^{-6} log^C = X T V^{-6} * lambda^3 l^{-3} log^C, whose dyadic sum is dominated by V ~ X^{1/3}: X*T*X^{-1} * l^{C-3} = T * l^{C-3}. Since N = T*l/2pi, this is o(N) iff the net log power C < 4 — an exact-constant question in Huxley's theorem (IK Thm 9.15) that the proposal flags as unverified; with the proposal's own coarser stated form n(V) << N T^eps X V^{-6}, the zone contributes N T^eps, which is NOT o(N) and certainly not N T^{-delta}. Consequences: the headline fixed-lambda tail theorem, the quantitative zero-density corollary, and the 'lambda -> 3/5 horizon' narrative all overstate what the displayed inputs deliver. The near-critical part (ii) is NOT hit by this finding (it avoids Huxley entirely) — but part (i) as stated is wrong and must be deleted or downgraded to a polylog-loss statement contingent on Huxley's exact log exponent.

findings.claim: The bridge lemma's additive error term O(T^{1/2} l), being V-independent as stated, makes BOTH parts (i) and (ii) of Theorem 1 non-sequiturs: it licenses cubic tail mass ~ T^{5/4} l >> N = T l at the top of the spectrum, and every downstream capacity argument rests on the ladder holding up to lambda_max.
findings.argument: Theorem 1(0) states #{i: |lambda_i| >= CV} <= C L |{tau: smoothed mass >= cVl}| + O(T^{1/2} l) with the additive term independent of V. The maximal eigenvalue is a priori lambda_max ~ X^{1/2} polylog = T^{lambda/2} polylog (Schur bound via sup|A| <= 2 sqrt(X); equivalently a depth-1/2 off-line pair contributes ~ X^{1/2}). Assembling T_3(V0) = Sum_dyadic V^3 #{lambda_i in [V,2V)} with the stated count, the additive floor contributes at the top level V ~ lambda_max: (T^{lambda/2})^3 * T^{1/2} l = T^{3lambda/2 + 1/2} l, which at lambda = 1/2+ is T^{5/4} l — exceeding N = T l by T^{1/4} (and worse at larger lambda; verified numerically). The Frobenius bound cannot rescue it: Sum_{>=W}|lambda|^3 <= lambda_max * kappa N via Frobenius alone, which is the very divergence the theorem exists to beat. So the proof sketch proves neither (i) nor (ii): the Schatten-3 conclusion requires a V-DEPENDENT error (or a proof that the error term's eigenvalues are bounded), which the sketch does not contain and which is nontrivial precisely at large V where the Prop 4.2 tail factors X^{1/2} = T^{lambda/2} live. This is repairable in principle (edge-window excision, rank bookkeeping with V-dependent thresholds), but it is the single load-bearing analytic gap: findings 4's 'clean ladder at all V up to lambda_max' — the only thing that gives the cubic row any asymptotic bite — is exactly what this hole leaves unproven.

findings.claim: The unconditional cubic budget c_3(lambda') contains asymptotically ZERO triple-correlation information — the genuinely cubic prime resonance is an absolute constant (~2.316) contributing o(N) — so the row's arithmetic input is bandwidth-one pair-correlation data, and the proposal's Alternative-Hypothesis evasion ('consumes triple-correlation data at combined Fourier support 3lambda' ~ 3/2, exactly the data class that distinguishes worlds') is false as an information claim.
findings.argument: Expand the prime side of tr G-hat'^3 in powers of the prime term P: (delta + P)^3 gives delta^3 (mean density geometry), delta*P^2 (a pair-type diagonal reading Sum Lambda(n)^2/n ~ L^2/2, i.e. the form factor F(alpha) on the band, exactly the data class tr^2 already reads with a different weight), and the genuinely cubic P^3 resonance n1*n2 = n3 over prime powers <= X. By unique factorization, n1 n2 = n3 with all three prime powers forces the SAME prime: p^a * p^b = p^{a+b}. Its total mass is Sum_p (log p)^3 Sum_{a,b>=1} p^{-(a+b)} = Sum_p (log p)^3/(p-1)^2 = 2.3158... — an absolute constant (computed numerically over primes to 3*10^6), versus the pair diagonal L^2/2 -> infinity. In the units where tr G-hat = N, this contributes O(N/l^3) = o(N). Off-diagonal near-resonances |log(n1 n2 / n3)| small are exactly what MV BOUNDS (never evaluates) inside the RS range X^3 <= T^{2-eps}, so they enter only as o(N) error. The zero-side pair part of the cubic reads F up to support 2lambda' = 1 + 2 theta loglog/log, but the weight mass on the sliver (1, 2lambda'] is O(loglog/l), i.e. o(N)-irrelevant. CONCLUSION: c_3(lambda') = [density term] + [F(alpha) on |alpha| <= 1 against an explicit weight] + o(N) — pure bandwidth-one pair data. Three consequences. (a) The AH evasion bullet is wrong: no world-distinguishing data class is consumed; any adversarial law matching zeta's band-1 pair data automatically reproduces the budget's VALUE, and pair-data-consistent worlds (AH-type laws included) remain fully relevant adversaries. (b) The only genuinely new content is the NONLINEAR (cubic-spectral) reading of the same data plus the count ladder — 'a nonlinear functional of bandwidth-one pair data', morally adjacent to the ceiling-covered class even though formally outside the Lean theorem's linear format. (c) The adversary's 3-point structure in the support hexagon is a free knob that NO consumed input constrains (only point-process realizability does): the equality row 'config's Sum lambda^3 = c_3 N' asks the adversary to tune one scalar with an infinite-dimensional position freedom. The proposal's honest prior already concedes budget = demand exactly at lambda = 1 (2 = 2); this finding removes the stated reason to hope lambda' near 1/2 is different.

findings.claim: The M2 decision gate is unsound as specified (marks {1,2} + CUE-sampled moments, no capacity row), and a sprinkling adversary shows the cubic row is asymptotically VACUOUS at theta >= 1 and retains bite at theta < 1 only through an LP-with-marks-up-to-W plus an O(N/W) fuzz row — i.e. the odd-moment no-go is evaded not by 'tail bound + sign' as claimed but only by the clean V^{-4} count ladder, which rests on the unproven bridge (finding 2).
findings.argument: Capacity analysis. Given the count ladder n(V) <= c(T) N V^{-4}, an adversary can shift the cubic equality row by adding on-line clusters of multiplicity m (positive shift) or deep-pair clusters (negative shift, costing nothing at lambda' since no inertia rows run there) at density n: cubic shift n*m^3, Frobenius/pair-row cost n*m^2, trace cost n*m, objective cost n. (I) At theta >= 1 the slice loss makes c(T) >= (loglog T)^2 (the proposal's own n_1 bound), and the choice m = loglog T, n = eps N/m^2 with eps = 1/sqrt(loglog T) satisfies the count row (eps <= (loglog)^2/m^2, verified numerically), costs eps*N = o(N) in Frobenius and pair rows, o(N) in trace and objective, stays below the V0 = (loglog)^3 tail cutoff — and swings the cubic row by eps*N*m = N*sqrt(loglog T) -> unboundedly more than the Theta(N) double-vs-pair signal. The cubic row at theta >= 1 is therefore satisfiable/neutralizable at asymptotically zero cost: the §7.5(e) no-go ('mass at height h -> infinity feeds m_3 freely') reasserts itself because V0 -> infinity is 'unbounded support' in the only sense that matters (per-unit-cubic cost at height V0 is 1/V0 -> 0). Theorem 1(ii)'s theta > 1 branch is decorative and the (loglog)^3-cutoff headline is a red herring. (II) At theta < 1 strictly, the slice loss (log T)^{2theta-2}(loglog)^2 = o(1), the ladder is clean (c(T) = O(1)), and the total cubic capacity from mark scales >= W is Sum_dyadic m^3 * c N m^{-4} ~ 2cN/W -> so the row CAN retain Theta(N) bite modulo an O(N/W) fuzz — this is the correct, narrower version of the evasion, and it is contingent on finding 2's bridge repair holding at ALL V. (III) Gate unsoundness: the specified N4 rerun of the 256-law LP with marks {1,2} forbids exactly the mark-m sprinkling the true asymptotic adversary is allowed — a 'ceiling break' outcome can be a pure artifact of the mark cap (false positive); conversely without the O(N/W) fuzz row a finite-N 'bites' outcome does not survive T -> infinity. And N3's CUE-sampling hard-codes GUE triple-correlation structure the adversary is not bound by (finding 3c). The gate must be re-specified: marks up to W, an explicit capacity/fuzz row, adversarial 3-point freedom subject only to realizability. Expected direction of the corrected computation, given finding 3 and the designer's own 2=2 admission: absorption, i.e. the no-go branch.

findings.claim: The sign-split discrimination (tight pair charges 4 units of negative Frobenius mass, double charges 0) is a per-isolated-block statement that fails under adversarial clustering: PSD on-line mass lifts a pair's negative eigenvalue toward 0 (annihilation), Sylvester gives only n_- <= p (never a lower bound), and the needed visibility lemma is the same configuration-free visibility theorem the campaign record argues is impossible — so Step 4's 'different corners of the constraint polytope' smear back together against the worst-case adversary.
findings.argument: The Step 4 separation requires reading, from the spectrum of G-hat', that a tight off-line pair contributes negative mass ~4 while an on-line double contributes none. But the matrix is a SUM of blocks: adding a PSD block (on-line cluster) to a hyperbolic pair block can only raise eigenvalues (Weyl), so an adversary placing each tight pair inside an on-line cluster drives its negative eigenvalue toward or past 0 — the campaign's own measurements found the honest compressed index identically 0 for X = 10^2..10^6 while sign-based predictions gave hundreds, and Part I argues (uncertainty-principle heuristic, empirical annihilation laws L*_ann) that no configuration-free visibility theorem exists. The certificate must be valid configuration-by-configuration, i.e. against the clustered presentation; then the only unconditional rows left are n_-(G') <= p and the global moment equalities. The proposal half-concedes this (M3b listed as 'the genuinely hard new mathematics'; failure mode 3's fallback drops the visibility lemma) but does not follow the concession to its conclusion: in the fallback, the negative-spectrum rows (Sum_-|lambda|^3 <= V0 Sum_- lambda^2, power-mean, n_- <= p) are correct linear algebra but toothless for the double-vs-pair separation, because the adversary's pair-rich configuration simply presents with Sum_- ~ 0 — indistinguishable in every surviving row from the double-rich configuration except through the cubic equality, which is finding 3+4's one nonlinear scalar of bandwidth-one pair data with O(N/W) fuzz. The lemmaR_tight degeneracy is therefore NOT broken by anything currently provable in the proposal; at best it is dented by the repaired M2 LP, whose outcome is genuinely open but adversely indicated.

findings.claim: Assorted smaller defects: the bridge 'converse' direction is unproven (signed-vs-absolute smoothing), Theorem 1(ii)'s count-bound threshold is inconsistent with its own ledger, and numerics N1 cannot distinguish the predicted regimes at accessible heights.
findings.argument: (a) Theorem 1(0)'s converse ('every such tau lies within O(1/L) of a window supporting an eigenvalue >= cV/C') does not follow from the Rayleigh argument: the diagonal entry G_kk is the SIGNED phi-hat-smoothed integral, while the ledger controls smoothed |A|; A has band L, so it can rotate a full phase period within one 2pi/L window and partially cancel. Harmless for the tail theorem (only the forward direction is used) but stated as part of the theorem. (b) The count bound in (ii) is stated 'for all V >= (loglog T)^3', yet the Chebyshev ledger proves it for all V >= C — and finding 4 shows the range below (loglog)^3 is where the leverage battle actually happens; the statement should claim what the proof gives. (c) N1 proposes T = 10^5..10^6 to validate tail exponents and falsify via 'stable slope -2'; but at T <= 10^6, (loglog T)^3 ~ 17 while lambda_max ~ T^{1/4} ~ 18-32 — the cutoff scale and the top of the spectrum coincide, so the asymptotic regimes the prediction separates are not resolved at accessible heights (consistent with the map's warning that all finite-T certificate quantities are far from asymptotic). N1 as designed can neither validate nor falsify the mechanism. (d) For balance: I verified the free fourth-moment diagonal Sum(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2/m = 2(Sum Lambda^2/n)^2(1+o(1)) = L^4/2 (unique-factorization argument is correct, same-prime coincidences are O(1)), the slice variance v_1 = theta*l*loglog T, the n_1 slice bound, the power-mean and Frobenius-split rows, and the dimension-cap and kappa evasions (counting only at lambda = 1) — these parts are sound.

result.repairs: (1) Bridge: restate Theorem 1(0) with a V-dependent error term and prove the count ladder up to lambda_max ~ X^{1/2}; if the error floor cannot be beaten below the N V^{-4} envelope at large V, restrict the theorem's V-range and add an explicit top-spectrum interpolation — this is the one analytic repair everything else depends on. (2) Delete Theorem 1(i)'s 'In particular' clause or downgrade it to a polylog-loss statement conditional on the exact log power in Huxley's theorem (o(N) requires net log power < 4 in my accounting; the T^eps form never suffices); drop the quantitative fixed-lambda zero-density corollary accordingly. (3) Fix the operating regime to theta < 1 strictly and state that theta >= 1 has no certificate value (sprinkling adversary). (4) Re-specify the M2 gate before trusting it in either direction: exact-rational LP with marks up to W, an explicit O(N/W) cubic-capacity fuzz row derived from the repaired ladder, adversarial triple-correlation freedom subject only to point-process realizability (not CUE sampling), and the sign-split rows evaluated on clustered/annihilated presentations. Only that LP is decision-relevant; a break in the marks-{1,2} rerun is not evidence. (5) Reframe the claims honestly: the route is 'a nonlinear spectral reading of bandwidth-one pair-correlation data with quantitative high-spectrum capacity control', not 'unconditional consumption of triple correlation'; strike the AH data-class bullet. (6) Keep and foreground the genuinely defensible deliverables: repaired Theorem 1(ii) as a standalone first-of-its-kind spectral-tail statement, the MD(lambda, delta) problem statement for the large-values community, and the sharpened no-go publication if the corrected M2 shows absorption — the proposal's own pricing of that branch is its most robust feature.
